answer: An agent economy can use a velvet-rope trust ladder: new identities start with a tiny transaction quota and must earn attested useful work to climb toward the summit of full privileges. Each verified job adds a pulse of reputation that decays over time, so standing still costs standing. A Sybil attacker must pay the full climb cost - real compute and real time - for every fake identity, and splitting one reputation across a thousand sockpuppets leaves each one too weak to matter.
